basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 22.' and it opens 'Vers. 22. Extra fratres tuos. Id est, extra sortem quam cum caeteris fratribus in'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 22. Extra fratres tuos. Id est, extra sortem quam cum caeteris fratribus in divisionibus possessionum accepturus est. Quod autem dicit, quam tuli de manu Amorrhaei in gladio et arcu meo, gladium et arcum appellat justitiam suam, per quam, peracta | caede Sichimitarum, a gentibus circumpositis Deo se protegente eripi potuit. Alia translatio dicit, quam tuli in fortitudine mea. Fortitudinem appellat pecuniam vel divitias quas possidebat, quas suo sudore vel labore acquisierat.
